4.text: Petr and Paskal were with me too. Petr was slouching on the couch on the right side of the office and staring at the ceiling. Paskal sat across from me. He was also eagerly waiting for the results.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: The whole process had been tough on all of us. But now there was nothing left to do but wait for the Justices to cast their vote.

6.speaker: Petr Vectern
6.text: "What do you think Anton? Are we going to make history today?"

9.speaker: Player
9.text: "To be honest, I have a bad feeling about this."

10.speaker: Petr Vectern
10.text: "So you trust Isabel to bring the votes?"

11.speaker: Player
11.text: "Yes. I'm sure she will support the proposal."

12.speaker: Player
12.text: "I don't know. But we have to hope for the best."

14.speaker: Narrator
14.text: Petr stared at the ceiling again.

34.speaker: Narrator
34.text: Petr was with me, slouching on the couch on the right side of the office and staring at the ceiling.

38.speaker: Petr Vectern
38.text: "But I guess the important person in all this is Heron..."

39.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
39.text: "But anyway, we'll learn about the vote soon. The session is already underway."

43.speaker: Petr Vectern
43.text: "I hope Lucian managed to talk some sense into him."

45.speaker: Player
45.text: "I hope so too. We'll see soon enough."

46.speaker: Player
46.text: "I trust Lucian. I'm sure we have Heron."

49.speaker: Petr Vectern
49.text: "But anyway, we'll learn about the vote soon. The session must have started already. What time is it?"

50.speaker: Narrator
50.text: I looked at the tall case clock in the room. It was already twenty past eleven. The Court's voting session was scheduled to end in ten minutes.

55.speaker: Narrator
55.text: Petr slowly turned his head from where he was slouching to see the clock.

57.speaker: Petr Vectern
57.text: "Okay. We'll soon hear about the results then."

58.speaker: Petr Vectern
58.text: "Maybe you shouldn't have pushed the Court so much... Taking away their immunity was a bit too aggressive."

59.speaker: Petr Vectern
59.text: "By the way, what time is it?"

60.speaker: Narrator

67.speaker: Petr Vectern
67.text: "Okay. We'll soon hear about the results then."

72.speaker: Petr Vectern
72.text: "I wouldn't blame them if they vote no."

74.speaker: Player
74.text: "What's done is done. There's no point in going on about it."

81.speaker: Narrator
81.text: He yawned and stretched out on the couch.

83.speaker: Narrator
83.text: He rose from his slouch and stretched.

87.speaker: Petr Vectern
87.text: "I don't know if you noticed, but Kesaro has been getting popular in the Assembly recently."

88.speaker: Petr Vectern
88.text: "Our party's been supporting him on a lot of bills, some of which have already reached you."

89.speaker: Petr Vectern
89.text: "What do you make of this? I think he's a very dangerous man, Anton. We can't let him divide our party."

90.speaker: Player
90.text: "I agree. We have to watch him closely."

91.speaker: Player
91.text: "I have no problem with bipartisan bills passing the Assembly."

92.speaker: Player
92.text: "I don't make anything out of it. It's expected that he'd get the support of our conservative wing."

93.speaker: Petr Vectern
93.text: "His party only holds 40 seats, Anton. Yet he manages to pass bills..."

94.speaker: Petr Vectern
94.text: "Maybe we shouldn't allow our party to be so generous with what they support..."

95.speaker: Player
95.text: "I don't make anything out of it. It's expected that he'd get the support of our conservative wing."

96.speaker: Player
96.text: "I have no problem with bipartisan bills passing the Assembly."

97.speaker: Petr Vectern
97.text: "I don't know if you noticed, but Kesaro has been very popular in the Assembly as of late.

98.speaker: Petr Vectern
98.text: "Our party's been supporting him on a lot of bills, some of which have already reached you."

99.speaker: Player
99.text: "I agree. We have to watch him closely."

100.speaker: Petr Vectern
100.text: "What do you make of this? I think he's a very dangerous man, Anton. We can't let him divide our party."

101.speaker: Petr Vectern
101.text: "Maybe we shouldn't allow our party to be so generous with what they support..."

102.speaker: Petr Vectern
102.text: "His party only holds 40 seats, Anton. Yet he manages to pass bills..."

104.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
104.text: "Mr. Kibener aside, we seem to be in a very troubling situation regardless."

105.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
105.text: "I don't want to be so negative right as we're waiting for the results but..."

106.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
106.text: "The political violence on the streets is not stopping. I am not sure if this was the right time for reform..."

107.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
107.text: "With the decrease in our law enforcement budget, I am feeling very stressed about the future of our country, Mr. President. Mrs. Morgna and Mrs. Graf seem to be under a lot of stress."

111.speaker: Petr Vectern
111.text: "And we've got enough trouble aside from him."

112.speaker: Petr Vectern
112.text: "The violence on the streets hasn't stopped since we came in. I am not sure if this is the right time for reform anymore, Anton..."

113.speaker: Petr Vectern
113.text: "I don't want to be so negative while we're waiting for the results, but..."

114.speaker: Petr Vectern
114.text: "With the decrease in our law enforcement budget, I'm not sure if this is ever going to stop."

115.speaker: Narrator
115.text: Suddenly, Livia entered the room. In her hands was a large object wrapped in straw paper.

116.speaker: Livia Suno
116.text: "Good day to you, Mr. President. Am I interrupting anything?"

119.speaker: Player
119.text: "No. Please come in. Is there a problem?"

120.speaker: Livia Suno
120.text: "Good day to you, Mr. President and Mr. Beniwoll. Am I interrupting you?"

124.speaker: Narrator
124.text: Suddenly, Livia entered the room. In her hands was a large object wrapped in straw paper.

127.speaker: Player
127.text: "No. Please come in. Is there a problem?"

128.speaker: Livia Suno
128.text: "The Chief Justice has sent you this."

129.speaker: Narrator
129.text: She showed me the wrapped object.

130.speaker: Player
130.text: "Thank you, Livia. You can leave it on my table."

131.speaker: Player
131.text: "Really? From Orso Hawker? Bring it here."

135.speaker: Narrator
135.text: She walked up to the table and gave it to me. I immediately started to remove the wrapping to reveal a framed photograph.

137.speaker: Narrator
137.text: It was an old black and white photograph of Tarquin Soll posing on a destroyed tank in Holsord Square. The building behind him had thousands of bullet holes on it and the clearly readable slogan 'Victory is close' written on its walls.

138.speaker: Narrator
138.text: The date, 14 March 1929, was written in the corner with a black marker.

139.speaker: Livia Suno
139.text: "He's obviously trying to send you a message, but--"

141.speaker: Narrator
141.text: Noticing Petr on the couch, Livia reddened slightly. She gave a small wave, which Petr returned.

142.speaker: Narrator
142.text: As soon as she left the room, Petr came up next to me and took a look at the photograph.

144.speaker: Player
144.text: "Yeah. A picture of Tarquin Soll. What a nice present..."

146.speaker: Player
146.text: "This must be some kind of a message."

149.speaker: Petr Vectern
149.text: "Victory will be close, huh? Orso's getting ahead of himself."

150.speaker: Narrator
150.text: Suddenly, Lucian rushed into the room.

151.speaker: Lucian Galade
151.text: "Mr. President! The vote has been concluded."

158.speaker: Narrator
158.text: Petr jumped up and down like a little kid.

160.speaker: Narrator
160.text: Petr put his hands on his forehead.

169.speaker: Petr Vectern
169.text: "This is a historic moment, Anton! We have changed Soll's Constitution of 1929... I am without words."

174.speaker: Player
174.text: "It's not the end of the world."

178.speaker: Petr Vectern
178.text: "That stupid photograph from Orso too! They are mocking us..."

179.speaker: Lucian Galade
179.text: "I'll talk to the cabinet and arrange a meeting immediately. We have to plan our next steps."

180.speaker: Lucian Galade
180.text: "This failure will not reflect well with the public or the Assembly..."

181.speaker: Player
181.text: "I am more scared of the Court. I'm a target for them now."

182.speaker: Player
182.text: "We will get through it. This was just a failed proposal."

184.speaker: Lucian Galade
184.text: "True. Mr. Hawker is the most dangerous of them all."

185.speaker: Petr Vectern
185.text: "I really want to believe in that..."

190.speaker: Narrator
190.text: Petr approached to give me a hug.

194.speaker: Lucian Galade
194.text: "Congratulations, sir. Today is a big day."

195.speaker: Narrator
195.text: All of us immediately got to work to plan our next steps after our Supreme Court failure.

196.speaker: Lucian Galade
196.text: "You must also start preparing a speech to announce the changes, sir."

197.speaker: Lucian Galade
197.text: "I'll go ahead and reach out to the cabinet. We can celebrate this together over a meeting."

198.speaker: Narrator
